ConnectDesk · Micromart Africa

From call centre to command centre

A blueprint for ConnectDesk as a modern collections floor: an auto-dialler with four calling modes, timed breaks, an 08:00 schedule, a supervisor who can move any seat to any bucket, and a phone with AI agents working every call. Phase 1 is built and running today as a simulation on Micromart's real book. This document says what is real, what is simulated, and what it takes to make each piece real.

Date22 September 2026
ForPhoebe Iminza, Collections
ReplacesCollectBox (CallBox)
StatusPhase 1 live, simulated

The change in one line

CollectBox records what agents typed after the fact. ConnectDesk runs the floor while it is happening. Every seat, every line and every break is visible on one screen. The supervisor can change any of them from that screen, and the dialler follows rules she sets once in settings.

What Phoebe sees in the demo

A control strip on every page

Top centre of every ConnectDesk screen. It holds the master dialler switch, live-call count, who is ready, on break, late back, paused or absent, and a red alert naming whoever has overrun a break.

The Command Centre

Every seat as a live tile. Break watch with countdowns that turn red. Buckets with the agents on them, schedule adherence for the day, and a floor log. Any seat opens into controls: pause, move, change mode, recall, listen, whisper, barge.

Dialler settings

Break types and their allowances. The daily schedule, with the dialler auto-starting at 08:00 and stopping at 17:30. Pacing, ring time, wrap-up and retry rules. Bucket routing, with a default mode for each book.

The Riri phone

An iPhone-style handset, bottom right. Every Call button opens it and dials. Agents can also dial by hand from its keypad. A co-pilot transcribes the call, catches the promise and writes the wrap-up.

Said plainly in the room: the agents, their extensions and the seven buckets with their loan counts are read live from CollectBox. Seat states, calls, breaks, the transcript and the AI metrics are a Phase 1 simulation, and every screen carries a Simulated badge. The late logins, the overrun washroom break and the absentee are scripted, even though they are shown against real agent names.

01

The control strip — the floor, one glance up

The strip sits in the header of every ConnectDesk page, so the floor is visible from the queue, a case file or the promise board without navigating anywhere. It has two faces, for two roles.

The supervisor's face

  • Dialler live / paused: one click pauses or starts the dialler for the whole floor. Pausing stops the next call; calls already in progress are allowed to finish.
  • Live counts: each count links into the Command Centre already filtered to those seats.
  • Late alert: a red pill naming whoever is furthest over a break, with the overrun ticking up, e.g. "+20:13 Washroom". It rotates through everyone who is late.
  • View as: step into any agent's seat and see exactly the strip that agent sees. Actions taken there are logged as that agent's.

The agent's face

  • Status and timer: Ready, Dialling, Previewing, On call, Wrap-up, Dialler paused, each timed from the moment it began.
  • Start / Pause dialler, and the dial mode menu (Predictive, Progressive, Preview, Manual), limited to the modes the supervisor allows.
  • Bucket: the agent sees which book they are on and who put them there. Only the supervisor can move them.
  • Logged in time and duration, dials and promises today.
  • Break: the menu lists the supervisor's configured breaks with their minutes and how many are left today. Picking one starts the countdown.

On a break, the strip becomes the countdown

Amber while the break is inside its allowance, with the time left and a progress bar. Red once it runs over, showing the overrun and "supervisor alerted". I'm back ends the break, logs any overage against it and returns the seat to the dialler.

02

The Command Centre — Phoebe's floor

The six numbers

  • Live calls now: concurrent calls, with a ten-minute sparkline.
  • On the floor: seated against rostered, late logins, absentees.
  • Dials today and connect rate.
  • Promises today and their value.
  • On break against the break cap, how many are over time, and total minutes over today.
  • Dialler: seats dialling, seats paused, pacing ratio.

The seat wall

One tile per agent: extension, login time (amber if late), status with a live timer, the customer on the line or the pause reason, bucket, mode, dials and promises. A tile over its break allowance turns red. Filters: on call, ready, on break, late back, paused, absent. Tick several tiles to move them to a bucket, change their mode, pause or start them in one action.

Break watch

Everyone on a break, most-late first. Each row shows the break type, allowance and start time, a countdown or a red overrun, and a Recall button once they are over.

Buckets

PRE, DUE, W1, W1M, W2, W3 and NPL with their real CollectBox loan counts. Each shows how many agents are on it, how many are live and the default dial mode. Clicking a bucket filters the seat wall to it.

Schedule adherence

Every agent against the 08:00 roster: login time, minutes late, breaks taken, time used against time allowed, minutes over, time paused, dials, connects, promises, talk time. The table is sorted with the worst exceptions first.

Floor log

Every login, break, overrun, pause, move and promise, stamped with who did it. Filters: breaks, supervisor actions, money.

03

One seat, opened — what the supervisor can do

ControlWhat it does
Pause / Start diallerPauses a seat with a reason (Coaching, Quality review, System / headset issue, Meeting, Disciplinary) or restarts it. The reason is shown on the agent's tile and in the log.
Recall from breakEnds the break on the supervisor's authority. The overage is logged as a recall against that break.
Move to bucketReassigns the seat to any of the seven books. The seat switches to that bucket's default dial mode.
How it dialsPredictive, Progressive, Preview or Manual, for this seat only.
Listen · Whisper · BargeOn a live call: listen silently, speak to the agent only, or join the call. Logged as a monitoring event.
End callThe supervisor can end a live call.
View as agentThe header strip becomes this agent's strip.
Log in / Log outManage the seat's presence on the floor.

The drawer also shows the day's figures (login time and lateness, dials, connect rate, promises, cash recovered from CollectBox, breaks used and over), every break with its allowance and overage, and the seat's own timeline.

The four calling modes

ModeHow it callsDefault for
PredictiveDials ahead of the agent at the pacing ratio (1.6 lines per ready agent by default) and connects only calls a human answers. Backs off above the abandon-rate cap.W1, W2 — high volume, reminder-led
ProgressiveOne number per free agent, dialled the moment they go ready. No abandoned calls.DUE, W3, W1M
PreviewThe case file opens first; the agent reads it, then presses call.NPL, PRE — negotiation and retention
ManualThe agent chooses who to call and dials by hand, from the Riri phone's keypad.Callbacks, escalations
04

Dialler settings — the rules the floor runs on

Break types

The supervisor sets each break's name, icon, allowance in minutes, how many a day, and whether it is paid. Out of the box:

BreakAllowedPer day
Tea break15 min2
Lunch45 min1 (inside 12:30–14:30)
Washroom5 minno limit
Prayer10 min1
Coaching / training20 minno limit
Supervisor meeting15 minno limit
System / headset issue10 minno limit

The allowance is the countdown the agent sees and the line that "late back" is measured against. Change the washroom allowance from 5 to 7 minutes and every countdown on the floor re-measures when you save.

The daily schedule

  • Working days Monday to Saturday, shift start 08:00, 5 minutes' grace before a login counts as late.
  • The dialler starts itself at 08:00 for every seated agent, and stops at 17:30. Nobody has to stand up and tell the floor to start.
  • A break cap (20% of seated agents at once) and auto-pause for an idle seat after 3 minutes.

Dialling and routing

  • Default mode, the modes agents may choose, pacing, abandon-rate cap, ring time (25 s), wrap-up (30 s), attempts per number per day (3), a calling window (08:00–19:00), answering-machine detection, call recording.
  • A default mode per bucket, and the order the dialler drains buckets in for a seat with no assignment.
05

The Riri phone — today's dialler, with AI on every call

The console's Riri handset has been ported to ConnectDesk, bottom right, and given a call centre's job. Every Call button on the desk fires one event, desk:dial. That includes the green button on each queue row and the Call button on a case file. The phone opens, unlocks and dials. Agents can also type a number on its keypad, or press Dial next in W1 to take the next customer from their bucket.

The call

  • Calling, ringing, connected, with the customer's band, days past due, amount due and loan number.
  • Mute, keypad, speaker, add (conference the guarantor), hold, record, transfer, end.
  • A call placed from the phone puts that agent's seat on call on the Command Centre too. The handset and the wall are one floor.
  • Clicking the customer on the agent strip opens the dialler's current call on the phone.

After the call

Riri writes the summary and picks the disposition from what was said, e.g. "Promise to pay — KES 3,200, Thursday". It adds a QA score and a compliance check. Save & next call files it.

Eight AI agents on the floor

AgentJob
Riri Co-pilotTranscribes the live call, reads the customer's mood, suggests the next line
Riri VoiceAI voice agent placing courtesy reminders on PRE and DUE
Promise detectorHears a commitment, extracts amount and date, books the callback
Auto wrap-upWrites the summary and the disposition

Compliance watchFlags threats, abuse and third-party disclosure as they are said

06

What is real today, and what is simulated

PieceTodaySource, or what makes it real
Agents and extensionsRealCollectBox UserMaster via the leaderboard, and the extension table. /api/desk/roster, read once per browser session.
Buckets and loan countsRealCollectBox tracker, the same rollup as the Live floor.
Cash recovered per agent todayRealCollectBox PayedAmount, shown in the seat drawer.
Seat states, timers, breaks, loginsSimulatedPhase 2: persisted seat sessions and break logs, driven by the agents' own clicks. No telephony needed.
Supervisor controlsSimulatedPhase 2: the same actions as server routes, audited.
Calls, dials, connectsSimulatedPhase 3: PBX click-to-call and CDR; Phase 4: the predictive engine.
Transcript, co-pilot, wrap-up, QAScriptedPhase 5: streaming speech-to-text (English and Swahili) and an LLM over the transcript.
Saved dispositionsNot writtenPhase 3: written back to CollectBox through the existing shadow write queue.

How the simulation runs. A pure state engine (lib/desk/dialler/sim.ts) advances the floor once a second in the browser. One tab leads and the others follow over a BroadcastChannel, so the projector and a second window show the same floor. State lives in the browser's local storage. Settings survive a reload; a new day re-seeds the floor. The shape of that state is the contract for Phase 2: when the dialler is real, server events replace the engine's tick and the screens above it do not change.

07

The build plan — making each piece real

The phases are ordered so each delivers value on its own. Phase 2 needs no telephony at all, and it is where most of Phoebe's control becomes real.

Phase 1 — The shell, simulated

DONE · 22 SEP

Everything in this document: control strip, Command Centre, Dialler settings, Riri phone, the event contract, on real agents and buckets.

Phase 2 — Real floor control, without telephony

NEXT
  • Tables: DeskSeatSession (login, logout, device), DeskSeatState (status, since, paused by, reason), DeskBreakType, DeskBreakLog, DeskSchedule, DeskBucketRoute, DeskFloorEvent. Org-scoped, audited.
  • Routes: POST /api/desk/seat/:id/{login,logout,pause,start,break,back,recall,assign,mode}, PUT /api/desk/settings/…, and a live stream (GET /api/desk/floor/stream, server-sent events) the strip and Command Centre subscribe to.
  • A scheduler that starts and stops the floor at the configured times and raises the overrun alert. It runs as a cron or a small worker, not in anyone's browser.
  • Agent accounts: each CollectBox agent gets a ConnectDesk login with an agent role, so the agent face of the strip is theirs.
  • Result: real login times, real breaks and lateness, real pauses and bucket moves, a real adherence report. It works even while agents still dial from their desk phones.

Phase 3 — Click-to-call on Micromart's PBX

NEEDS PBX ACCESS
  • ConnectDesk already reads the extensions and CDR (the Phone floor page). The next step is originating calls: a Call button rings the agent's extension, then bridges to the customer (preview and progressive modes).
  • The Riri phone becomes a WebRTC softphone registered as the agent's extension, for agents without a desk handset.
  • Every call is tied to its CDR and recording. Dispositions are written back to CollectBox through the shadow write queue.
  • Needs from Micromart: PBX admin/API access, a SIP trunk or confirmation of the existing one, and a recording store.

Phase 4 — The predictive engine

AFTER PHASE 3
  • Pacing against ready agents, answering-machine detection, the abandon-rate cap, attempts per number per day, the calling window, and draining by bucket priority.
  • Live monitoring (listen, whisper, barge) through the PBX's spy and conference features.

Phase 5 — AI on every call

AFTER PHASE 3
  • Streaming speech-to-text for English, Swahili and Sheng. An LLM over the rolling transcript for next-line suggestions and promise extraction, and for the wrap-up, disposition and QA score once the call ends.
  • Compliance watch: flags for threats, abusive language and disclosure to a third party, with the clip attached.
  • Riri Voice: an outbound voice agent for courtesy reminders on PRE and DUE, handing any customer who wants a person to a live agent.
  • Propensity and best-time-to-call ranking, from the payment history ConnectDesk already reads.

Phase 6 — Workforce management

LATER

Rosters and shift swaps, call-volume forecasts by hour, break planning against the forecast, and an adherence export for payroll and commission.

Before any recording or transcription goes live: customers must be told calls are recorded, and recordings are personal data under Kenya's Data Protection Act, 2019. Retention, access and consent need to be agreed with Micromart before Phase 3 records its first call.

08

Demo run-sheet — ConnectDesk in ten steps

Signed in as Phoebe at connectdesk.servicesuitecloud.com/micromart. Open the Command Centre once before the meeting so the floor is warm.

  1. Any page. Point to the strip: "The dialler started itself at 08:00. Live calls, ready, on break, late back, paused, absent, on every page."
  2. The red pill. "This agent took a five-minute washroom break twenty minutes ago." Click it. The Command Centre opens with her seat.
  3. Recall. Press Recall. The tile goes back to work and the overage is logged in the floor log.
  4. Break watch and adherence. Scroll to who logged in late and the minutes over against allowance for the day.
  5. Move a team. Tick three tiles, then Move to bucket, NPL. They switch to Preview mode.
  6. Pause the floor. Press Pause the floor: "calls in progress finish". Then start it again.
  7. View as an agent. Open any seat, then View as agent. The strip shows the agent's face. Take a Tea break and watch the countdown. Click I'm back.
  8. Settings. Change Washroom from 5 to 7 minutes and save. The overrun on the floor re-measures.
  9. Call. Work queue, then the green Call button on any row. The Riri phone opens and dials. Riri transcribes, catches the promise and writes the wrap-up. Save.
  10. AI floor. On the phone's home screen, open AI floor: "Eight agents working beside the people."

If anything misbehaves: Dialler settings, then Reset the floor, rebuilds this morning's floor in a second and keeps the settings. The seat names can be switched to a sample team in the same card.
